QF.id: AIFM CIII Fee Structure and Fund Performance_45

question.text: Mr. Ramesh Iyer (CFO of a Cat III AIF) is structuring incentive fee crystallisation. Which frequency is MOST COMMON for Cat III open-ended AIFs in India?

answer.text: Monthly, quarterly or annual crystallisation with payment typically at period-end (sometimes deferred to the end of fund term for close-ended)
Crystallisation only on full fund liquidation
Only on investor redemption with no periodic crystallisation

explanation.text: The Logic: Typical Cat III practice: incentive fees ACCRUE daily (so NAV is clean for sub/red) and CRYSTALLISE monthly, quarterly or annually depending on PPM. Close-ended Cat III may defer payment to end of term; open-ended pays at crystallisation period + on redemption. The Trap: A is operationally impractical. C is Cat I/II-style. D partially true but not 'most common'. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-B Cat III Distributor covers frequency conceptually; XIX-E covers accounting mechanics. Manager's Pro-Tip: When crystallising, also CRYSTALLISE the new HWM at the same date. A lag between carry payment and HWM reset is a classic double-dip audit finding.
